newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: LIBERAL LEADER CALLS ON HOWARD TO FACE REPUBLIC ISSUE
New South Wales Liberal Opposition leader Peter Collins has called on the Howard government to act on the republic when Cabinet resumes today.
Mr Collins told a meeting of republicans in Adelaide last night the biggest hurdle to a republic was that older Australians feared change would threaten the value of their contribution to the nation.
However, he said cutting ties with the British government posed no threat to Australia's heritage.
Mr Collins advocates a simple progression towards a republic with a president replacing the Governor General.
LIGHTNING STRIKE VICTIM IN CRITICAL CONDITION
A 42-year-old woman is in a critical but stable condition at a Melbourne hospital following yesterday's fatal lightning strike.
Samir Guirguis, aged 42, and his wife, 39-year-old Salma Guirguis, were killed by the lightning strike at Eastern Park in Geelong yesterday morning.
A group of about 20 adults and 10 children, from the Arabic Baptist Church in Coburg, were having a barbecue when the rotunda they were sheltering in was struck by lightning.
Several other people were treated for burns and shock.
Family members are caring for the dead couple's children, two boys aged 10 and 12.
VICTORIAN NATIONAL PARKS BURN AFTER LIGHTNING STRIKES
Firebombers are dumping tens of thousands of litres of retardant on fires started by lightning strikes in north-west Victoria's national parks.
Despite the efforts of the five aircraft, 10,000 hectares of public land are expected to have been burnt by the end of the day.
Firefighters say they're expecting continuing problems, with more lightning activity expected during the next few days.
HUNT ON AFTER CROC CLOSES CAIRNS BEACHES
Environment department officials and crocodile farmers are meeting this morning to work out how to catch a three-metre crocodile that's forced the closure of four Cairns beaches.
Acting Regional Director Lindsay Delzoppo says trapping the crocodile will be difficult because it is wandering over a wide area.
She says she hopes the crocodile is caught before the 30-day permit for its capture runs out.
The permit for the commercial farm to catch the crocodile is the first issued under the new Estuarine Crocodile Management Plan.
COMBINATION VACCINE OFFERS LESS PAIN, FEWER SIDE EFFECTS
A new combination vaccine to immunise children against five diseases, including whooping cough, is expected to be available by the end of the year.
It's currently being trialled by the Westmead Children's Hospital in Sydney.
Dr Margaret Burgess, professor of paediatrics at the hospital, says the vaccine has been specially developed to prevent side effects.
She says the new vaccine should provide greater encouragement for parents to immunise their children, with just one injection needed on each occasion.
The new vaccine will give protection against diphtheria, tetanus, hepatitis B and HIB meningitis.
TORRES STRAIT SMUGGLING A FOCUS OF PNG TALKS
Federal Customs Minister Geoff Prosser will look at upgrading pursuit boats to catch smugglers in the Torres Strait, but Australia won't be re-negotiating the Torres Treaty with Papua New Guinea.
The Minister recently visited the Torres Strait and held talks with PNG officials.
Mr Prosser believes drug smuggling could be better combated with more co-ordination between authorites and smaller faster boats.
QUEENSLAND CITY TO BAN PIT BULLS
Toowoomba city councillors are confident that pit bull terrier dogs will be banned in Toowoomba after tonight's council meeting.
The Toowoomba City Council will consider changing local laws to ban all new pit bull terriers and terrier types.
The Community and Environmental Services Committee chairman, Councillor Phil Connole, says the law will also ban all pit bulls being brought in to the city.
He says the council will have the ability to seize a dog and order its destruction.
